parsed.incumbent_segment: Exhaustive closed-receptacle-first search visiting all cabinets and drawers before inspecting open surfaces and stoveburners
parsed.warrant: The incumbent performed an exhaustive 28-step search prioritizing closed cabinets and drawers before reaching open surfaces and stoveburners, directly contradicting the established memory's open-surface-first guidance. The trajectory proves only that exhaustive search is feasible here, not that it is optimal. Since pans are strongly associated with stoveburners and open surfaces, resolving whether a targeted or open-surface-first policy reduces search cost is highly policy-relevant.

parsed.guidance: Navigate to an available cooking appliance first. If the target cooking vessel is observed there, take it. If not, fall back to inspecting available open horizontal surfaces, then closed storage receptacles. Stop searching as soon as the target is observed.
parsed.hypothesis: For cooking vessels requiring downstream cooling, prioritizing navigation to cooking appliances (e.g., stove burners) before inspecting general open horizontal surfaces or closed storage receptacles reduces total search actions by targeting semantically likely spawn locations first.

probe_spec.adaptive_policy: From the entry state, select an available cooking appliance from the admissible actions and navigate to it. Inspect the resulting observation for the target cooking vessel. If found, take it and terminate the search. If not found, select an available open horizontal surface and navigate to it, repeating the inspection. If still not found, select a closed storage receptacle, navigate to it, open it, and inspect. Terminate immediately upon first target observation.
probe_spec.evidence_goal: Whether navigating to a cooking appliance first yields the target cooking vessel in fewer total search actions than starting with open horizontal surfaces or closed storage receptacles.
probe_spec.local_function: Search environment receptacles to locate and acquire the target pan object.
